About us

We Fix The Leak. We Do Not Rip Out Your Bathroom.

A leaking shower rarely needs a full renovation. In most Sydney homes the water is escaping through failed silicone, cracked grout or a tired membrane, and all three can be treated from the surface with specialist leaking shower repairs. No demolition, no skip bin in the driveway and no re-tiling bill at the end of it. Depending on what the inspection finds we reseal a leaking shower, re-grout the shower or renew the bathroom waterproofing underneath — whichever is the real leak. We also carry out bathroom leak repair where the water is escaping beyond the shower itself.

Good to know

Leaking Shower Repair FAQs

Can you fix a leaking shower without removing the tiles?
In most cases, yes. The majority of shower leaks come from failed silicone, cracked grout or a worn waterproofing membrane at the junctions, and all of those can be repaired from the surface with no demolition or re-tiling.
Why is my shower leaking?
Usually it comes down to worn sealants or faulty tiles. Silicone perishes, grout cracks as the building moves, and the membrane underneath eventually gives up. An inspection will tell you which one it is.
How long does a leaking shower repair take?
A typical repair takes a few hours, depending on the issue. Most resealing and regrouting jobs are finished in a single visit and the shower is usually ready to use again within 24 hours.
How much does a leaking shower repair cost?
Costs vary with the cause and the size of the shower, and repairing early usually saves money. We give you a fixed scope quote after an inspection, so you see an itemised price before any work begins.
Will I need to replace my tiles?
Not always. Tiles are only replaced if they are damaged or if they are the source of the leak itself.
Do you provide a waterproofing certificate?
Yes. Every completed waterproofing job comes with a certificate, along with our 100% workmanship guarantee.
Is mould a sign of a leaking shower?
It can be. Constant dampness behind tiles and in the surrounding rooms creates the conditions mould needs, so recurring mould is worth having inspected.
How often should shower sealants be replaced?
Every one to two years as a general rule, or sooner if you start seeing leaks, lifting silicone or dark staining along the joints.
Do you service all of Sydney?
Yes. We cover all 33 Sydney local government areas and we come to you. Tell us your suburb and we will confirm the next available inspection.
Do you work with strata and commercial properties?
Yes. We regularly handle residential, commercial and strata or body corporate bathroom and balcony leaks right across Sydney.
